description: An eight-panel composite (4 rows × 2 columns) comparing predicted DRX kinetics of "Model 2" (left column) with the "3D CA" model (right column); the two column headers are printed at the top. All eight panels share identical axes: y = DRX fraction (0.0-1.0, ticks 0.2) and x = True strain (0.05-0.9, ticks at 0.1). Rows (a) and (b) are annotated "Temperature: 950°C" and vary strain rate — solid black 0.01s⁻¹(Constant), solid purple 0.1s⁻¹(Constant), red dashed 0.01s⁻¹-0.1s⁻¹ (a) or 0.1s⁻¹-0.01s⁻¹ (b) at 0.2 strain, and the matching cyan dashed history at 0.4 strain. Rows (c) and (d) are annotated "Strain rate: 0.01s⁻¹" and vary temperature — solid purple 950°C(Constant), solid black 1050°C(Constant), red dashed 1050°C-950°C (c) / 950°C-1050°C (d) at 0.2 strain, cyan dashed at 0.4 strain. Filled circular markers on the dashed curves are annotated "0.2 strain", "0.3 strain", "0.4 strain", "0.5 strain"; Model 2 panel (a) additionally prints transition strains "0.245 strain" and "0.437 strain". Model 2 dashed curves show abrupt kinks at the transition strain while the 3D CA curves remain smooth, which is the figure's argument.
measured_quantities: transition true strain (dimensionless, printed values 0.245 and 0.437)

observations.observation: The figure is an eight-panel composite arranged as four rows (a)-(d) by two columns, with printed column headers 'Model 2' (left) and '3D CA' (right).
Every panel uses the identical axes: y = DRX fraction from 0.0 to 1.0 (ticks at 0.2) and x = True strain from 0.05 to 0.9 (ticks at 0.1 from 0.1 to 0.9).

Rows (a) and (b) are annotated 'Temperature: 950°C' and compare strain-rate histories: solid black 0.01s⁻¹(Constant), solid purple 0.1s⁻¹(Constant), red dashed 0.01s⁻¹-0.1s⁻¹ (a) / 0.1s⁻¹-0.01s⁻¹ (b) at 0.2 strain, and cyan dashed versions of the same history at 0.4 strain.

Rows (c) and (d) are annotated 'Strain rate: 0.01s⁻¹' and compare temperature histories: solid purple 950°C(Constant), solid black 1050°C(Constant), red dashed 1050°C-950°C (c) / 950°C-1050°C (d) at 0.2 strain, and cyan dashed same history at 0.4 strain.
In every Model 2 panel the dashed varying-condition curves show an abrupt kink/step at the marker strain, whereas the corresponding 3D CA dashed curves are smooth and continuous.

Model 2 panel (a) prints the transition strains '0.245 strain' (magenta, on the red dashed 0.2-strain curve) and '0.437 strain' (blue, on the cyan dashed 0.4-strain curve); the paired 3D CA panel (a) labels the same events only as '0.2 strain' and '0.4 strain'.
Filled circular markers placed on the dashed curves are annotated '0.2 strain', '0.3 strain', '0.4 strain' and '0.5 strain' in rows (c) and (d).
In row (c) the constant 1050 °C curve lies to the left of the constant 950 °C curve, i.e. it reaches a given DRX fraction at lower true strain, so the higher deformation temperature accelerates DRX.

In the 3D CA panel (d) the red dashed 950°C-1050°C (0.2 strain) curve reaches DRX fraction close to 1 at approximately the 0.3 true-strain gridline, at lower strain than the 1050°C(Constant) black curve, showing a temperature increase strongly accelerates DRX.
No numeric DRX-fraction values are printed anywhere in the group; the only printed non-axis numbers are the transition strains 0.245 and 0.437 in panel (a) Model 2.

The model comparison is symmetric: rows (a)/(b) reverse the strain-rate direction (increase vs decrease) and rows (c)/(d) reverse the temperature direction (drop vs rise), each evaluated at switch strains of 0.2 and 0.4.
The supplied caption is only '(caption on next page)', so no caption-supplied values, sample names or processing details can be attached to this figure group.

The paper title and abstract place this figure in a study of multi-stage (varying-condition) recrystallization in low-alloy steel modelled with an inhomogeneous-dislocation-density 3D cellular automaton, comparing it against an earlier model.
